text.p: Zinc prices roared higher during the latter part of Wednesday afternoon LME trading, as the speculative froth currently underpinning the market continued unabated. Trends elsewhere on the LME were mixed at the close, although a resilient copper market absorbed a mid-afternoon setback and was little changed on renewed spread tightness, traders said.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 1.28 points to 237.42.
On the LME, zinc was the main performer, snapping back up from an abortive dip under $1,450, and racing up to a closing high of $1,463, a $26 advance from Tuesday's kerb close.

In copper, July option declarations this morning passed smoothly, with the July date falling harmlessly between strikes at $2,500 and $2,550. Subsequent unwinding of unneeded option hedge cover pushed prices down to a low of $2,368 before renewed tightness in the spreads prompted a rally. Last three months trade was at $2,390, down just $3 a tonne.

Aluminium again defended the $1,600 level when necessary as the market continued to tackle overhead resistance and producer selling. Last trade was at $1,610, up $7, with further gains anticipated if stock drawdowns are maintained, traders said.
Nickel prices rebounded during the latter part of the session, with the market climbing back above $6,900 to close at $6,940, up $10.

Lead partly recovered from an early afternoon sell-off back under $630, which traders said reflected a profit-taking reaction to recent gains. Nevertheless, the flip back above $630, which was due to trends in other markets, still left prices $4 lower at $632.
Tin met some support under $5,500, and closed with a modest $5 gain at $5,535. Alloy was indicated at a higher $1,458/63 a tonne.

IPE Brent crude futures shrugged off early losses on Wednesday prompted by disappointing U.S. inventory data to end firmer on a wave of short-covering, dealers said. August Brent, which tested support at $18.50 a barrel in early dealing, closed 12 cents firmer at $18.92 after touching a high of $18.96. After running up smartly on Tuesday in anticipation of bullish U.S. data, modest losses had been expected from the open given the smaller than expected draw in key refining regions.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on signals the market was oversold, traders said. Also, there were ideas the market may have found its seasonal bottom after the recent fall to contract lows and three-year lows, they said. CBOT soft red winter wheat closed one to three cents per bushel higher, with July up 1-1/2 at $3.24 per bushel. September was up one at $3.32-1/2.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower across the board Wedneday, led again by gold which slid to new four-year lows. "The consensus is universally bearish in gold, and with producer hedging apparent, against a backdrop of seasonally slow demand during the summer, any upward correction will likely meet overhead selling," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said. COMEX August gold ended down $2.80 at $332.20 an ounce, after seeing a further life-of-contract low at $332.10 near the close. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $331.10/60, after seeing a London afternoon fix at $332.15. Earlier gold had fixed at $331.45 at the morning fix, the lowest since March 24, 1993. In New York Tuesday, spot gold had ended around $333.70/20.
